title: Why Speculative Decoding Works Better Than Predicted on Sparse MoE Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.38981v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) accelerates autoregressive inference by leveraging the memory bound nature of decoding, verifying multiple draft tokens in a single forward pass. For mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, prior work predicts a concave speedup-batch size relationship, with gains peaking at intermediate batch sizes due to expert saturation. We evaluate this across 10 sparse MoE models (30B--1T parameters, 8--512 experts) and find recent fine-grained models break this trend, showing higher speedup at low batch size. We find verification cost is governed not only by activated-expert bytes, but also by temporal overlap across draft tokens and GPU execution dynamics. At low batch size, MoE layers in fine-grained models account for a much smaller share of runtime than of weights; on H100, kernel profiling attributes this mainly to higher bandwidth utilization of MoE kernels relative to attention, with L2 absorbing repeated reads of co-rou

translated_title: 为什么推测解码在稀疏MoE模型上的效果优于预期
translated_abstract: 推测解码通过利用解码过程内存受限的特性来加速自回归推理，在单次前向传播中验证多个草稿token。对于混合专家模型，先前的工作预测加速比与批大小之间呈凹形关系，由于专家饱和，增益会在中等批大小时达到峰值。我们在10个稀疏MoE模型（参数量300亿至1万亿，专家数量8至512个）上对这一预测进行了评估，发现近期的细粒度模型打破了这一趋势，在低批大小时展现出更高的加速比。我们发现，验证成本不仅由激活专家的字节数决定，还受草稿token之间的时间重叠以及GPU执行动态的影响。在低批大小时，细粒度模型中MoE层在运行时间中的占比远小于其在权重中的占比；在H100上，内核性能分析将其主要归因于MoE内核相对于注意力机制具有更高的带宽利用率，且L2缓存吸收了对共同路由（co-rou……）的重复读取（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文通过在10个稀疏MoE模型上的实证评估，发现细粒度MoE模型在低批大小时推测解码的加速比高于先前理论预测，并揭示了验证成本不仅取决于激活专家的字节数，还受草稿token时间重叠和GPU执行动态（尤其是MoE内核更高的带宽利用率与L2缓存作用）的影响。
en_tdlr: Through empirical evaluation across 10 sparse MoE models, this paper shows that fine-grained MoE models achieve higher-than-predicted speculative decoding speedups at low batch sizes, revealing that verification cost depends not only on activated-expert bytes but also on temporal overlap across draft tokens and GPU execution dynamics, particularly the higher bandwidth utilization of MoE kernels and L2 cache absorption.
